title: Sessao de worker morta no primeiro turno queima o teto de timeout inteiro e reporta causa falsa: 30 minutos por um erro de 5 segundos
description:
MEDIDO DUAS VEZES EM 40 MINUTOS na sessao de 2026-07-30, dispatchando o plano do CAM-478. Responde a pergunta que o CAM-477 deixou explicitamente em aberto e adiciona um custo que ele nao mede.

OCORRENCIA 1: planner spawnou 06:21:15.797Z (spawn-resolution, uuid a251d32e-9453-4205-b0c2-09c44563b2cf). O event log registrou dispatch-failed as 06:51:20.183Z com {phase: planner-timeout, paneId: %44, exitCode: 1, stderr: can't find pane: %44, reason: pipe-pane-exited}. Exatamente 30 minutos, o teto. O TRANSCRIPT DA SESSAO, porem, tem 9 linhas e 3414 bytes no total, e a unica linha de assistant e: 'API Error: 529 Overloaded. This is a server-side issue, usually temporary'. Ou seja a sessao morreu na PRIMEIRA chamada de API, poucos segundos apos o spawn, e o supervisor esperou os 30 minutos inteiros antes de perceber.

OCORRENCIA 2, o re-arm imediato: planner spawnou por volta de 06:56Z (uuid c50547bc-d8b0-4f9c-9561-52aff057af2b), pane %45. Transcript identico em forma: 8 linhas, 3121 bytes, prompt do usuario seguido de 'API Error: 529 Overloaded' e nada mais, congelado desde 06:58:20Z. O processo claude (pid 25751) continuou VIVO e o pane continuou presente, entao desta vez nem sequer houve pane sumido: a sessao esta viva, inerte e segurando o slot ate o teto.

DOIS DEFEITOS DISTINTOS, AMBOS MEDIDOS:

(1) CUSTO: nao existe deteccao de morte precoce. Qualquer falha de primeiro turno (529, quota, erro de rede, prompt rejeitado) custa o teto INTEIRO de 30 minutos, mesmo quando o sinal de morte esta disponivel em segundos. O sinal ja e conhecido e ja esta documentado no proprio projeto: o mtime do transcript da sessao e o sinal de liveness (memoria claude-p-buffers-transcript-liveness). Um transcript que para de crescer com 8 linhas, tendo como ultima entrada de assistant um 'API Error', e distinguivel de trabalho em andamento em menos de um minuto. Em modo autonomo isso e a diferenca entre um retry de 1 minuto e meia hora parada por ciclo, e o erro upstream em questao e explicitamente transiente ('usually temporary').

(2) CAUSA REPORTADA E FALSA. O rotulo emitido foi planner-timeout com reason pipe-pane-exited. Nenhum dos dois descreve o que aconteceu: nao houve timeout de trabalho (nao houve trabalho nenhum) e o pane sumido e consequencia, nao causa. A causa real (529 no primeiro turno) existe SOMENTE no transcript e nao chega a lugar nenhum que o loop leia: nem ao event log, nem ao marker, nem ao push pro orquestrador. Um orquestrador autonomo lendo apenas o event log concluiria que o planner e lento ou que o issue e grande demais, e a acao corretiva obvia (reduzir escopo, aumentar o teto) seria exatamente a errada. Esta e a mesma doenca do CAM-435 (pane-died do implementer descarta a causa: quota esgotada), agora confirmada tambem no planner e com o agravante de que aqui a causa e transiente e o retry correto e imediato.

RELACAO COM O CAM-477: aquele issue registra a terceira ocorrencia do dispatch-failed com pane sumido e SUGERE, sem decidir, investigar 'se o caminho de timeout mata o pane antes de tentar pipe-pane sobre ele, o que faria a causa ser ordem interna e nao corrida externa'. A evidencia aqui responde: nao e corrida estreita de TOCTOU entre o check e o uso. Na ocorrencia 1 a sessao estava morta ha ~30 minutos quando o handler rodou, e na ocorrencia 2 o pane nem sumiu. O pane sumido do CAM-477 e sintoma tardio de uma sessao que morreu no inicio, nao de uma corrida no instante do dispatch. Este issue nao substitui o CAM-477 (que trata da robustez da operacao de tmux em si) nem o CAM-440 (pane ocioso segurando o mutex), mas os dois deveriam ser lidos junto com este.

NAO E DEFEITO DE PLANEJAMENTO NEM DO CAM-478: a main estava limpa, o issue era plannable, e o mesmo dispatch subiu normalmente quando a API respondeu. A causa e integralmente upstream; o defeito nosso e de deteccao, de custo e de honestidade do rotulo.

DIRECAO SUGERIDA, NAO DECIDIDA: (a) checar liveness por mtime e crescimento do transcript da sessao spawnada, com um piso curto (ordem de 60 a 120s sem crescimento apos o primeiro turno) antes de declarar morte precoce, em vez de esperar o teto; (b) ao declarar falha, extrair a ultima entrada de assistant do transcript e propaga-la como causa no event log, no marker e no push, para o rotulo parar de mentir; (c) tratar 529 e demais erros transientes com backoff e re-spawn automatico, distinto de um timeout real de trabalho, que nao deve ser re-tentado da mesma forma.

spec.scope: IN SCOPE, one coherent change at one shared fix site: teach the dispatch wait path to read the spawned session's own transcript, and use that single read for two things at once. (1) EARLY-DEATH DETECTION: a pure predicate that recognises a session that died on its first turn (transcript frozen across a floor window whose last assistant entry is a transient API error) so the wait ends at the floor instead of the cap, wired into all four poll loops (implementer loop.ts:1400-1470, reviewer review.ts:566-608, planner plan-runner.ts:1137-1168, auditor plan-runner.ts:1182-1201). (2) TRUE-CAUSE PROPAGATION: the extracted cause text travels into the dispatch-failed event, the durable marker, and the orchestrator push, so the recorded label stops lying. Plus the three measured record-integrity defects at that same site: planner pane-death is currently reported as poll COMPLETION and degrades to a terminal with no reason field at all; auditor pane-death and cap-elapsed return a byte-identical bare failure and are both labelled auditor-timeout; and the emitted phase field carries a synthesized reason string (phase: 'planner-timeout'). EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE, each with a reason: automatic re-spawn or any change to retry POLICY, because the retry envelope already exists (MAX_DEAD_WORKER_RETRIES=4) and is merely starved by 30-minute attempts, so failing fast makes it effective without new logic and without runaway risk; the respawn-pane -k before pipe-pane ordering and remain-on-exit, which is CAM-477; pane-scrape evidence capture and wiring the existing unwired quota classifier in src/retry/patterns.ts, which is CAM-435 and stays open; the idle-pane mutex, which is CAM-440. This issue does NOT close CAM-435 or CAM-477.
acceptanceCriteria: A pure predicate classifies a spawned session as dead-on-first-turn from its transcript alone: a transcript whose byte size has not grown across the floor window AND whose last assistant entry is a transient API error reports early-death, while a still-growing transcript, or one whose last assistant entry is normal work, reports still-working. [oracle: bun test ./test/supervisor/dispatch-early-death.test.ts -t "classifies a frozen transcript whose last assistant entry is an API error as dead-on-first-turn"]

The detector is consulted inside each of the four dispatch poll loops (implementer, reviewer, planner, auditor), so a first-turn death ends the wait at the floor instead of the cap: driven with an injected clock, each loop reaches its failure terminal at under ten percent of its configured cap. [oracle: bun test ./test/supervisor/dispatch-early-death.test.ts -t "every dispatch poll loop ends an early-death wait far below its timeout cap"]

The cause text extracted from the transcript reaches the durable dispatch-failed marker as its own field, so a reader of the marker alone learns why the dispatch failed without opening any transcript. [oracle: test $(grep -c cause src/supervisor/dispatch-failed-marker.ts) -ge 1]

A single new reason literal session-died-early joins the shared DispatchFailureReason union and is the reason emitted for an early death in every phase, rather than one ad hoc label per phase. [oracle: test $(grep -c session-died-early src/supervisor/verified-dispatch.ts) -ge 1]

Planner pane death before prd.json exists is no longer reported as poll completion: it yields a reason-bearing terminal instead of the bare planner-failed terminal that carries no reason field at all. [oracle: bun test ./test/supervisor/plan-runner-early-death.test.ts -t "planner pane death before prd.json yields a reason-bearing terminal, not bare planner-failed"]

The auditor poll loop returns distinguishable results for pane death versus cap elapsed, instead of one byte-identical bare failure for both, and the caller labels each with its own cause. [oracle: bun test ./test/supervisor/plan-runner-early-death.test.ts -t "auditor pane death and auditor cap elapsed are distinguishable at the poll boundary"]

The emitted phase field carries only a real phase name and never a synthesized reason string, so the event log stops recording phase values like planner-timeout. [oracle: test $(grep -c "phase}-timeout" src/supervisor/plan-runner.ts) -eq 0]

The eight pre-existing DispatchFailureReason literals keep their observable-terminal contract (event plus marker plus notification) unchanged. [oracle: bun test ./test/supervisor/verified-dispatch.test.ts]
gotchas: DO NOT ADD RETRY LOGIC. The envelope already exists and is merely starved: MAX_DEAD_WORKER_RETRIES=4 (loop.ts:774), NO_PROGRESS_BACKOFF_MS=60000 (loop.ts:689), MAX_BACKOFF_MS=300000 (loop.ts:699). Today a first-turn-dead implementer burns 4 x 30 minutes of cap before its dead-worker terminal. Failing fast makes the existing envelope effective; adding a second retry mechanism on top would compound it.

The supervisor-to-transcript dependency ALREADY EXISTS and must be reused, not duplicated: src/supervisor/events.ts:29 already imports parseTranscriptUsage and transcriptPathForSession from ../transcript/usage.ts for token accounting. The resolver is transcriptPathForSession (src/transcript/usage.ts:232-235), yielding <claudeDir>/projects/<encoded-cwd>/<uuid>.jsonl. Do not write a second path resolver.

The uuid needed to resolve the transcript is ALREADY on every failure path: DispatchFailedMarker carries a uuid field (src/supervisor/dispatch-failed-marker.ts:16-24) and the uuid is stamped on every emitted event. Nothing structural blocks the read; the reason the cause is lost today is simply that nobody reads it.

All four poll loops share one exit set (report-file present, pane_dead, cap elapsed) and NONE has an elapsed-time floor or first-turn probe: loop.ts:1400-1470, review.ts:566-608, plan-runner.ts:1137-1168, plan-runner.ts:1182-1201. Fix the shared shape; do not special-case one phase.

Liveness today rests on exactly ONE signal, tmux display-message -p pane_dead (host.ts:583-592, consumed loop.ts:1403, review.ts:573, plan-runner.ts:1157 and :1195). It is provably insufficient: in the second measured occurrence the dispatch-failed event carried exitCode 0 and an EMPTY stderr because the pane stayed alive and inert for the full 30 minutes. Do not add another pane-derived signal expecting it to help.

pipe-pane out-logs are WRITE-ONLY: paths are built at worker-dispatch.ts:44-46 and plan-runner.ts:735 and there are ZERO readers anywhere in src/. Do not substitute 'read the out-log' for the transcript read without first proving the out-log is populated at the moment of failure.

pollPlannerDeath returns TRUE on pane death (plan-runner.ts:1157-1158), making pane death indistinguishable from prd.json completion. The caller then produces { kind: 'planner-failed' } (declared plan-runner.ts:282) which has NO reason field at all. Both halves must change together, or the cause is extracted and then discarded at the type boundary.

pollAuditorReport returns a byte-identical bare { ok: false } for BOTH pane death (plan-runner.ts:1196) and cap elapsed (plan-runner.ts:1197-1199), and the caller labels both auditor-timeout (plan-runner.ts:1364-1366). An auditor dying 5 seconds after spawn is currently reported as a 30-minute timeout.

The plan timeout path emits TWO dispatch-failed events for one failure: the inner one from verified-dispatch.ts:116-122 (invoked at plan-runner.ts:1070) carrying phase 'planner-timeout' plus reason 'pipe-pane-exited', and the outer one at plan-runner.ts:1105-1119 carrying phase 'planner' plus reason 'planner-timeout'. The marker written at :1090 overwrites the inner. Measured: 6 of the 9 dispatch-failed events ever recorded carry a reason string in the phase field.
The synthesis that corrupts the phase field is ${phase}-timeout at plan-runner.ts:1064, passed as phase at :1072. That is the exact site the phase-integrity criterion measures.

A quota and rate-limit classifier ALREADY EXISTS in-repo and is UNWIRED: LIMIT_PATTERNS (src/retry/patterns.ts:31-40, including /usage limit/i at :36) and isRateLimited (:60-81). Measured: zero files under src/supervisor/ import src/retry/. Wiring it is CAM-435 and is OUT of scope here. Do not import it in this PRD.

Caps differ per phase and one is not 30 minutes: implementer host 30 min (loop.ts:650), implementer CONTAINER 60 min (loop.ts:662), reviewer 30 min (review.ts:343), planner and auditor 30 min (plan-runner.ts:219), plan poll interval 5 s (plan-runner.ts:216). Express the floor relative to the cap or as its own constant; hardcoding 30 minutes silently breaks container mode.
Every test must drive the injected clock, never wall time; existing precedent is test/supervisor/loop.test.ts:384 and :427. A test that actually waits out a floor makes the suite unrunnable.

remain-on-exit is set NOWHERE in the repo (measured: zero hits across src/, templates/, docs/), and the sentinel command is echo <reason> (loop.ts:1531, review.ts:599, plan-runner.ts:1075) which exits in milliseconds, so the pane self-destructs and pipe-pane then fails against a gone pane. That ordering is CAM-477 and is OUT of scope; do not 'fix' it here.

ORACLE KINDS ARE DECLARED, do not conflate them. The four named-test criteria are RED BY ABSENCE (bun test <file> -t <name> exits 1 when the name matches zero tests), so they are satisfied by the test existing and passing; they are change detectors only insofar as the assertions inside them genuinely fail against the pre-fix code, which the implementer must confirm. The phase-integrity criterion is the only structural oracle that is RED BY BEHAVIOR (grep -c currently returns 1 and the criterion demands 0). The verified-dispatch criterion is a GUARD, green today by design, and must stay green.

The ./ prefix on the test-path oracles is REQUIRED and was verified in both directions: bun test ./path -t name exits 0 when file and name exist and 1 when the file is missing. Without the prefix bun treats a missing path as a name filter and emits a warning instead.

NEVER read an oracle's exit status through a pipe. bun test ... | tail reports tail's status, which turns a red oracle green. This trap was hit live while authoring this very spec and invalidated both controls until re-run without the pipe.
Orchestrator and worker scratch must NEVER be written inside the repo: any untracked file fails the plan preflight clean-tree guard. Use /tmp for payloads, probes and drivers.

COST BASELINE, measured from the event log on 2026-07-30, to carry into the PR body: a healthy planner produced a full PRD in 2m30s (spawn 07:43:20.115Z, auditor spawn 07:45:50.721Z), while two dead-on-first-turn planners each cost 30m04s (06:21:15.797Z to 06:51:20.183Z, and 06:54:43.957Z to 07:24:48.214Z). Across 1237 completed worker runs the median is 6.9 min and p90 is 18.0 min, so a 30-minute cap is 4.3x the median productive run. All 9 dispatch-failed events ever recorded are timeouts and all 9 landed within the last 3 days.

TRANSCRIPT SIGNATURE of a dead-on-first-turn session, measured twice: 8 to 9 lines, roughly 3.1 to 3.4 KB total, whose single assistant entry reads 'API Error: 529 Overloaded. This is a server-side issue, usually temporary', frozen from that moment on. That is distinguishable from work-in-progress in well under a minute, which is the entire basis of the floor.

CLAUDE_DIR RESOLUTION DECIDES WHETHER THIS FIX SHIPS INERT. Resolve the Claude config root exactly as src/supervisor/host.ts:1033 already does: process.env['CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR'] ?? join(homedir(), '.claude'). MEASURED IN THE LIVE ENVIRONMENT 2026-07-30: CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR is set to /Users/eduardo/.claude-pessoal, and the default ~/.claude/projects/<encoded-cwd> directory still exists but holds only June-era transcripts (13 files, newest 2026-06-07). A detector that hardcodes ~/.claude therefore resolves a real, readable, PERMANENTLY STALE directory: it never throws, never logs, and simply never fires. Any test must cover a claudeDir that is NOT the homedir default.

POSITIVE CONTROL for the detector, measured from a real healthy planner on 2026-07-30 (session d5f67a59): 70 entries, 256519 bytes, 16 tool_use blocks, accumulated over about 4.5 minutes, still growing when sampled. The detector MUST classify that as still-working. Contrast with the dead-on-first-turn signature of 8 to 9 entries and roughly 3.1 to 3.4 KB whose only assistant entry is an API error. The two are separated by more than an order of magnitude in both entry count and byte size, so the predicate does not need to be subtle, but it MUST be driven against both fixtures rather than the dead one alone.
domainTerms: early death: a spawned worker session that fails on its first API turn, before producing any work
floor: the short no-growth window after which a frozen transcript is declared dead, as opposed to the cap
cap: the per-phase timeout ceiling (30 min host, 60 min container implementer) that a wait may not exceed
poll loop: the per-phase wait loop that polls for a report file, pane death, or cap expiry
dispatch-failed marker: the durable JSON evidence file written at a failed dispatch, carrying phase, paneId, uuid, exitCode, stderr, reason
session transcript: the per-session .jsonl under the Claude projects dir, resolved from the uuid, already read for token accounting
sentinel respawn: the echo <reason> command respawned into the pane to force a terminal, which exits in milliseconds
observable terminal: the event plus marker plus notification triple that every dispatch failure must produce
red-by-absence: an oracle red only because the named test does not exist yet
red-by-behavior: an oracle red because an assertion genuinely fails against the current code
detector versus guard: a criterion that must fail pre-fix, versus one that is green today and must stay green
